status: Authored planned national reference; neither production forecast, legal mandate nor funded delivery

sectors.F: producing firms, including the assumed minority public portfolio

limits: All GDP, wage, consumption, capital, tax and physical quantities are authored assumptions.
Cash public service cost includes wages and purchases; public noncash depreciation enters GDP once and not a second cash bill.
Tax on products is 265/1800 of chosen tax-inclusive household consumption; paid compensatory relief 40 is a transfer, not a second product-tax deduction.
Other production tax 155 comprises land 100, ecological 15 and business 40 in the base; GDP income subtracts these before gross operating surplus.
Private taxable profit is residual surplus less private depreciation; dividends only use after-tax profit and the declared payout share.
No private corporate interest in this bounded fixture; equity claims equal its productive asset book value, not empirical market price.
Portfolio 25% is assumed validly owned at opening, not acquired by this record; raising it to 60% costs the stated book-price counterfactual and 5% debt carry.

Refundable credit alternative retains 25% additional gross work earnings after 10% contribution via one candidate 65% gross charge/needs credit; it does not adopt a new tax or automatic legal set-off.
All modeled capital dividends and household public interest go to 5000 high earners and face 40% personal capital charge; actual ownership and tax bases remain unknown.
The earned-pension branch pays 45 and holds restricted future liabilities unpriced; any financial insurance surplus stays reserved.
All flow entries are planned accrued transactions. An unfunded transfer/wage/supplier obligation is not paid or safely received; counterpart assignment of arrears is not modeled.
National energy/water cases add authored private demand to public demand, preserve standby/ecological allocations, and do not establish geography, safety, emissions or lawful rationing.
GDP 4500 and wages times 1.5 with fixed needs prices are a conditional affordability hypothesis, not proven real productivity, price behavior or an attainable transition.
Positive planned savings neither creates a lender commitment nor removes the cash limit.
Foreign reserves are separate, with exports/imports in invented matching units and fixed period conversion; no peg or actual counterparty consent is inferred.
Remaining function-level costs, land/material/emissions, qualified shifts, actor independence, source law and actual comparative wellbeing are unknown.
The 45% retained-work and 75% corporate-tax sensitivity is an authored alternative, not a selected rate or behavioral forecast; it exposes different household and enterprise financing needs.

A paid-portfolio operation assumes a separately authorized prior 672 debt/equity bridge. Its principal is not hidden in current tax revenue or counted as GDP; actual prior lenders/transfer are unverified.
